title: Testing a warehouse at peak load before it opens
lead: Space Data and Kasumigaseki Capital are studying three Japanese logistics sites. They want to see how buildings and equipment could handle a rush of incoming goods or a machine outage.

news.title: Washington is still seeking answers from NVIDIA’s interim leadership
news.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS that the administration had been in touch with NVIDIA’s interim leadership over chip shipments to China. He said he was still waiting for answers about who was responsible for complying with export rules.
news.details: Officials contacted the interim leadership, directors and lawyers.
news.technical_novelty: Bessent identified shipping and payment records as sources for reviewing the transactions.
news.engineering_impact: For buyers of computing capacity, the inquiry concerns procedures at a major supplier.
news.limitations: The public remarks assign no responsibility for violations and give no terms for future shipments.
news.evidence_status: CBS published the interview transcript and Reuters separately reported the contacts.
news.organization: US Department of the Treasury and NVIDIA
news.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent used a November 22 CBS interview to describe the administration’s questions about NVIDIA’s handling of chip shipments to China. He disclosed direct contact with people now overseeing the company. Officials want to know who was responsible for complying with export rules at the supplier and who knew about the transactions under review.

Bessent said the administration had contacted NVIDIA’s interim leadership, board directors and lawyers. At the time of the interview, he said it was still waiting for the answers it wanted. He said officials wanted to find out who was responsible for compliance with export rules and what levels of the company knew about shipments under scrutiny.

Bessent pointed to shipping and payment records as a way to reconstruct transactions even where arrangements were informal. He described possible systemic noncompliance as something still being looked into. Reuters also reported the contacts. NVIDIA’s board announced on November 12 that Jensen Huang had resigned and that chief financial officer Colette Kress would serve as interim CEO. Bessent confirmed that the chief financial officer was in charge.

A business buying computing capacity for robotics faces separate uncertainties about the rules for a transaction and whether its supplier can document the necessary approvals. The new information from Bessent concerns the latter: officials are seeking to establish who signed off and what records are available. A procurement manager still has no basis to revise a delivery forecast from this interview alone. It did not provide terms or a timetable for specific transactions.

news.title: Two Japanese partners want to test warehouse flows before fitting the equipment
news.summary: Space Data and Kasumigaseki Capital are exploring computer models for three Japanese logistics sites. They want early estimates of whether planned warehouses can handle peak demand and what happens if equipment stops.
news.details: The candidates include two planned automated warehouses and one existing site in Sakado.
news.technical_novelty: The proposed models would show how workers and goods move through each facility.
news.engineering_impact: Testing the layout early could expose problems that cost more to fix after installation.
news.limitations: The partners have not set a study timetable or estimated gains for individual sites.
news.evidence_status: The partners announced the study, and LNEWS reported the proposed sites.
news.body:
Japanese developer Kasumigaseki Capital and technology company Space Data have started looking at ways to design and operate warehouses using computer models. They named three candidate sites, including planned warehouses for ambient-temperature and frozen goods. They want to evaluate peak loads and the effect of equipment stoppages before work begins at the new facilities.

The partners identified three possible sites. Atsugi is the planned location for an automated ambient-temperature warehouse, and Fukuroi for a frozen-goods warehouse. The projects have target completion dates in spring 2029 and spring 2030 respectively. Landcube in Sakado is an existing facility where the partners are considering ways to link equipment and software.

The companies want to model buildings, equipment, workers’ movements and flows of goods. They would use the models to vary the placement and number of robots and transport equipment, check how much the system could handle at peak times and see what happens when equipment stops. The partners left the exact scope and schedule of the work open.

Warehouse automation is tied to the layout of the building. Fixing a bottleneck after opening could mean moving machinery or changing the routes workers use. The partners want to combine their experience designing and operating facilities with computer simulation. Sakado gives the study an existing site where they could examine how equipment and software already in place work together. The announcement says what the partners want to evaluate and gives no estimates for throughput or savings at individual sites.

news.title: Shinshiro tests which part of a medicine delivery can move from road to air
news.summary: Aichi Prefecture, Shinshiro and two companies tested three ways to fly medicines to recipients. One combined a road trip to the launch site with a flight, while another had pharmacy staff load the drone after it landed near them.
news.details: Green Service ran flights and Aeronext provided the operating system.
news.technical_novelty: A pharmacy can send a box to a hub or load the drone at a pickup stop.
news.engineering_impact: The trial tests where an existing medical logistics operator can take responsibility for flights and handoffs.
news.limitations: The partners did not disclose the full cost of regular deliveries.
news.evidence_status: The project partners described the trial, and industry outlet LNEWS reported on the routes.
news.organization: Aichi Prefecture, Shinshiro, Aeronext and Green Service
news.body:
Aichi Prefecture and Shinshiro worked with Aeronext and Green Service to see which part of a medicine delivery could move from road to air. The November 20 report sets out three routes. The practical question was whether a local company already in the business of delivering medicine could run the flights and organize handoffs to the recipients.

In the public demonstration on November 18, a pharmacy brought the medicine by road to the launch site at Yokogawa community center. The crew loaded a box onto the drone. According to the organizers, it flew about eight kilometers in roughly 12 minutes to a nursing home, where staff collected the package. The time given was for the flight from the launch site to the destination.

On a different route, the aircraft left the hub empty, landed near a pharmacy for staff to load a box and flew on to a second nursing home. The organizers put the two outbound legs at about 13 and five minutes respectively, excluding the return. Local medical logistics company Green Service ran the flights, with remote operations based in Tsushima.

The routes redistribute work. One requires an urban pharmacy to bring the box to a hub. Another has pharmacy staff wait for the drone and load the box where it lands. Aeronext provided the operating system and trained Green Service personnel, and the local company managed the flights. The individual flight times give the partners one part of the delivery economics. Comparing the service with driving would also require staff travel, waiting time and handling at the destination. The partners did not publish a full cost per delivery.

news.title: Arrive AI estimates equity above Nasdaq’s threshold after debt exchange
news.summary: Arrive AI, a US developer of parcel handoff stations for vehicles, drones and couriers, filed an update with the Securities and Exchange Commission. After several transactions, the company put stockholders’ equity at about $7.7 million against a Nasdaq minimum of $2.5 million.
news.details: Stockholders’ equity was $2,198,652 on September 30 before the adjustments.
news.technical_novelty: Lender Streeterville Capital received preferred stock in exchange for debt.
news.engineering_impact: For buyers of logistics equipment, the vendor’s ability to support installed delivery stations matters.
news.limitations: The estimate is unaudited, and final accounting for the debt exchange is pending.
news.evidence_status: The company’s November 20 Form 8-K filing and its investor release document the update.
news.body:
US parcel-infrastructure developer Arrive AI reported a change in its capital structure on November 20. The company estimated stockholders’ equity, the accounting value left after subtracting liabilities from assets, at about $7.7 million after several transactions. In its Form 8-K filing with the US securities regulator, it compared that with the $2.5 million Nasdaq minimum applicable to the company.

The company reported stockholders’ equity of $2,198,652 on September 30. It later took in $250,000 in gross proceeds from a private share sale and about $1.3 million through a program to sell shares at market prices. It also exchanged debt owed to Streeterville Capital for preferred stock, shares with rights defined by their issue terms. Arrive AI says it believes it again meets the stockholders’ equity requirement.

Arrive AI develops parcel handoff points where a courier, vehicle or drone can leave goods for a recipient arriving later. Customers relying on maintenance over the life of that equipment have a reason to track the vendor’s finances. The equity estimate applies the transactions as though they had taken place on September 30. It excludes subsequent operating results, and Nasdaq will continue to monitor compliance.

news.title: Bagel Labs’ two-arm model comes with terms for commercial evaluation
news.summary: Canada’s Bagel Labs published code and scores for a model that controls two robot arms. The results come from simulation, and companies need a separate paid agreement even to evaluate the model internally.
news.details: The RoboDojo-Sim computer test awards partial credit across five categories.
news.technical_novelty: Model weights, the numerical settings learned during training, are available for download.
news.engineering_impact: The license determines whether a company can include the model in an internal evaluation.
news.limitations: The developer has published no performance figures from a customer site in this release.
news.evidence_status: Licensing terms and simulation results are published by the developer.
news.body:
Toronto-based Bagel Labs released the code and weights for a program that uses instructions and camera images to work out how two robot arms should move. The release includes results from RoboDojo-Sim, a virtual test in which control programs operate simulated robots. The scores can help teams decide what to assess in more depth when the test tasks resemble the work they want to automate.

The model receives a task instruction, views from one head camera and two wrist cameras, and the robot's current state. It predicts 32 actions in a batch, executes 16 and then makes a new plan from fresh observations. That refresh lets the next prediction account for where the arms and objects are after the previous burst of movement.

In Bagel Labs' November 20 snapshot of RoboDojo-Sim, the model placed third among models evaluated without a separate software agent. It averaged 38.65 points out of 100, with an average full-task success rate of 31.91%. It completed 3.33% of trials in the Open category, which includes open-ended tasks and tasks guided by text or images. The ranking awards partial credit and gives each of the five main categories the same weight.

Downloading the weights, the numerical settings obtained during training, is straightforward. Permission to use them depends on who is doing the work. Bagel Labs’ documentation requires a separate paid agreement for companies or anyone acting on their behalf, including for internal research and benchmarking. That condition matters before a team commits staff time to an evaluation. A prospective user can also choose in advance which operations need to finish in full: the completion rate helps answer that question, while the published ranking rewards intermediate progress too.

technology_signal.title: Modeling the warehouse before equipment decisions
technology_signal.summary: Space Data and Kasumigaseki Capital want to simulate different numbers and positions of robots and transport equipment and see how much each layout could handle.
technology_signal.implications: The companies are still defining the study. Finding bottlenecks early could give them a chance to change a layout before installing machinery.
